details.note: Receipt carries contract_sha256 but NOT report_sha256. Per NEXARA governance pattern, receipts should cross-reference both frozen artifacts. Recommend adding report_sha256 field.

BRAIN_ABOVE_RUNTIME.evidence: Both components in src/nexara_prime/brain/. Dependency graph restricts to MemoryController + KnowledgeGraph. No runtime imports. protected_phase1_files block runtime.py.

MEMORY_FOUNDATION.evidence: Both components read via MemoryController.rank_retrieve() (exists in brain/memory_controller.py), write via MemoryController.commit() (exists with full signature). MemoryController enforces evidence binding for non-working layers.

EVIDENCE_BACKED.evidence: All capabilities specify evidence_kind. Both schemas include evidence_id column. MemoryController.commit() rejects EVIDENCE_REQUIRED_KINDS without evidence_id.

PERSONAL_SOVEREIGN.evidence: Contract explicitly states 'single-owner model — no federated learning, no telemetry'. Forbidden action #3: 'preference data leaves local environment'. No external system dependencies in dependency graph.

INCREMENTAL_ACTIVATION.evidence: Activation gates defined via AutonomousBoundary.check() but the action IDs ('preference_model_activate', 'experience_learning_activate') are NOT in any boundary set (ALLOWED/BLOCKED/APPROVAL_REQUIRED). They fall through to default-allowed. Furthermore, the contract uses string comparison '== ALLOWED' but check() returns a BoundaryDecision dataclass — the correct check is '.allowed == True'. See critical issues below.

PreferenceModel.note: commit() signature is (mission_id, key, content, kind, ...) — the contract shorthand 'commit(preferences)' is semantically correct as the kind='preference' binding

blocked_1_preference_auto_activate.finding: The activation gate checks AutonomousBoundary.check('preference_model_activate'). This action ID is NOT in AUTONOMOUS_BLOCKED, AUTONOMOUS_ALLOWED, or APPROVAL_REQUIRED sets. boundary.py defaults unknown actions to ALLOWED (response='PROCEED'). Verified by live boundary test: check('preference_model_activate') → allowed=True, response='PROCEED'. No human approval gate exists.
blocked_1_preference_auto_activate.recommendation: Add 'preference_model_activate' to APPROVAL_REQUIRED set in brain/evolution/boundary.py, OR add an explicit human-approval validation path in the activation sequence.

blocked_2_runtime_dispatch.description: experience patterns modify runtime dispatch logic
blocked_2_runtime_dispatch.finding: Both components are brain-layer only. Dependency graph restricts reads to MemoryController + EvidenceStore + KnowledgeGraph, writes via MemoryController.commit(). No runtime dispatch hooks. Protected Phase 1 files block runtime.py modification.

blocked_3_data_leaves_local.finding: Enforced by PERSONAL_SOVEREIGN principle and architectural isolation (brain layer, no external system imports). No explicit technical exfiltration guard — this is a policy-level constraint consistent with the design-only phase.
blocked_3_data_leaves_local.recommendation: During implementation, consider adding a data-egress assertion in MemoryController that verifies commit() target locality.

blocked_4_multi_user.finding: Acknowledged as out-of-scope design constraint. Single-owner model consistent with PERSONAL_SOVEREIGN principle.

blocked_5_weight_export.description: model weight export to external systems
blocked_5_weight_export.finding: Policy-level constraint. No export API defined in design. PreferenceModel.get_profile() returns PreferenceProfile for audit, not external export.
blocked_5_weight_export.recommendation: During implementation, ensure get_profile() output is for local audit only and does not serialize model internals.

issues: check() returns BoundaryDecision dataclass, not string. '== ALLOWED' would fail against an object. Correct: check(...).allowed == True
'preference_model_activate' not in any boundary set — defaults to allowed. No human-approval path exists despite contract claiming approval requirement.
Same BoundaryDecision vs string comparison issue.
'experience_learning_activate' not in any boundary set — defaults to allowed.

pattern_extraction_auto.contract_gate: BLOCKED — requires EVO-07 R3 capability gate
issues: Contract says BLOCKED but 'pattern_extraction_auto' is NOT in AUTONOMOUS_BLOCKED set. Live test: check('pattern_extraction_auto') → allowed=True. Implementation MUST add this to AUTONOMOUS_BLOCKED.

critical_issues.title: Activation gate string comparison is semantically wrong
critical_issues.description: Contract specifies 'AutonomousBoundary.check(...) == ALLOWED' but check() returns a BoundaryDecision dataclass, not a string. The condition would always evaluate False. Correct check: check(...).allowed == True or check(...).response == 'PROCEED'.
critical_issues.impact: Implementation following the contract literally would produce non-functional activation gates.
critical_issues.fix: Update contract and implementation to use check(...).allowed == True OR add __eq__ to BoundaryDecision that accepts string 'ALLOWED'/'PROCEED'.

critical_issues.title: Preference model activation lacks human approval enforcement
critical_issues.description: Forbidden action #1 states 'preference_model auto-activates without human approval'. But 'preference_model_activate' is not in AUTONOMOUS_BLOCKED, AUTONOMOUS_ALLOWED, or APPROVAL_REQUIRED boundary sets. boundary.py defaults unknown actions to ALLOWED. The activation gate would pass without any human interaction.
critical_issues.impact: PreferenceModel could activate autonomously, violating the design contract's primary forbidden action.
critical_issues.fix: Add 'preference_model_activate' and 'experience_learning_activate' to APPROVAL_REQUIRED set in brain/evolution/boundary.py. Alternatively, add a dedicated human-approval step before the boundary check.

warnings.title: pattern_extraction_auto not actually blocked in boundary
warnings.description: Contract says 'pattern_extraction_auto: BLOCKED — requires EVO-07 R3 capability gate'. But 'pattern_extraction_auto' is NOT in AUTONOMOUS_BLOCKED. Live test shows check() returns allowed=True.
warnings.fix: Add 'pattern_extraction_auto' to AUTONOMOUS_BLOCKED set in brain/evolution/boundary.py.

warnings.title: Receipt missing report_sha256 cross-reference
warnings.description: Receipt carries contract_sha256 but not report_sha256. Per NEXARA governance pattern, receipts should cross-reference both frozen artifacts for chain-of-custody.

warnings.title: EvidenceStore dependency at non-brain import path
warnings.description: ExperienceLearner reads from EvidenceStore which lives at src/nexara_prime/evidence.py (outside brain/). While EvidenceStore exists and is valid, importing from outside the brain layer could violate BRAIN_ABOVE_RUNTIME if evidence.py has runtime imports. Current evidence.py imports SQLiteStore, EventBus, and models — all infrastructure, not runtime. Acceptable but worth noting.
warnings.fix: Document in implementation contract that ExperienceLearner must import EvidenceStore through a brain-layer adapter to maintain isolation.

info.title: MemoryController.commit() signature not explicitly matched to contract shorthand
info.description: Contract says 'MemoryController.commit(preferences)' and 'MemoryController.commit(experiences)'. Actual commit() signature is (mission_id, key, content, kind, ...). The contract uses semantic shorthand (kind='preference'/'experience'). Implementation should use kind='preference' for PREF-01 and kind='experience' for EXP-01 to align with MemoryController's evidence-binding classification. The 'preference' kind is already in EVIDENCE_REQUIRED_KINDS — ensure 'experience' is added.

summary: NEXARA Phase 2B Design Contract is architecturally sound and well-structured. All 5 design principles have deliberate enforcement mechanisms. The dependency graph is valid — every declared dependency exists in the codebase. Both components have complete method specifications, schemas, and test targets. However, the review identifies 2 critical issues and 3 warnings that must be addressed before implementation: (1) the activation gate string comparison '== ALLOWED' is wrong — check() returns a BoundaryDecision dataclass, not a string; (2) the primary forbidden action 'preference_model auto-activates without human approval' is not enforced — the action IDs fall through to default-allowed in the boundary; (3) 'pattern_extraction_auto' is not in AUTONOMOUS_BLOCKED despite the contract declaring it blocked; (4) the receipt is missing the report_sha256 cross-reference; (5) EvidenceStore lives outside brain/ which merits an import-path note. The design is APPROVED_WITH_ISSUES — fix the 2 critical issues before proceeding to implementation.
next_gate: HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED — address CRIT-01 and CRIT-02 before NEXARA_PHASE_2B_IMPLEMENTATION
